architecture: v2 (architecture 2, re-root 2026-11-02: a new world, dataset and shell; a Nebraska city electric department's January 2027 patrol of Feeder 14, the line recloser's 2026 trips relocated through the main line's segment impedances)
slot_note: Re-root of the anomaly-detection slot. Architecture 1 (an investor-owned utility's underground cable failures) is spent on measurement and stays delivered on the portal. Architecture 2 moves to a new world (a city-owned electric department's overhead rural feeder), a new dataset and a new shell; the decisive step moves off any count of rows by key onto a per-trip relocation forced by the GIS segment impedances.
niche: a city-owned electric department locating what kept tripping its longest rural feeder's line recloser through 2026, for the one main-line section its January 2027 patrol walks, when the recloser's own fault locator carries the first conductor's impedance over a main line whose conductor changes partway out
analyst_test: A strong analyst who reads every field correctly maps the recloser's own fault-locator distances, which agree with every crew-found fault location on file to within a tenth of a mile, onto the main-line sections and sends the patrol to the section where the 2026 trips cluster in that record, about two miles beyond the fault.
domain_test: Protection engineering's fault location by apparent impedance decides the call: a fault's distance follows from its current and the cumulative impedance of the line between the source and the fault, which stops being proportional to distance where the conductor changes; with another field's nouns there is no impedance, conductor or fault current and the task does not read the same.
layer2_pattern: own:fault location on a non-uniform line
layer1: a recloser event export in local time across the November daylight-saving change, against the AMI head-end's UTC
fault currents in amperes in the event export and kiloamperes in the protection study
GIS segment lengths in feet against the patrol's miles and the study's miles
conductor carried by ACSR code name in the GIS and by size in the construction standards' impedance table, which sits inside a PDF
pole tags renumbered in the 2023 GIS conversion, the old tags still on older work orders
stakeholder_role: the electric department's system engineering group, which writes the January patrol order

spine.entity: one AMI meter event (power off, power on or momentary interruption) at one service meter

world.geography: United States, Nebraska (a fictional city, its electric department, substation, feeder and places)
world.org_type: a city-owned electric distribution department with long rural feeders

driver: A device records where each event arose by a calculation that assumes the line is uniform along its whole length, every check on file falls in the stretch where it is, and beyond a change in the line's make-up the calculation overshoots, so the place the events cluster in the device's record is not where they arise; only re-deriving each event's position from its raw measurement through the line's actual make-up, segment by segment, finds it.
driver_concrete: Each 2026 two-phase trip of Feeder 14's line recloser R1407 is relocated from its fault current through the GIS segment impedances (336.4 ACSR to the conductor change, 1/0 ACSR beyond), not read from the recloser's own fault locator, which carries the 336.4 impedance over the whole main line and so places the wind-day cluster about two miles too far out, while every crew-found fault on file lies on the 336.4 stretch where the setting is exact.
stump: A competent solver maps the recloser's fault-locator distances onto the main-line sections and sends the January patrol to the section where the 2026 trips cluster in that record, about two miles beyond the fault; the step that lands it there is trusting a single-impedance locator, validated only on faults inside its first conductor, on a main line whose conductor changes partway out.

differentiation.task186: task186 tests each fuel station's price change across an event against its own changes in quiet periods under shared local cycles (a noise model for a change); task183 tests no change: each recorded trip's position is re-derived from its fault current through the main line's segment impedances, because the recloser's locator assumes one conductor for the whole line

lineage.architecture: v1 (Tamsin Valley Electric's underground cable program: which of eight feeders fails most in 2027, from each section's own failure history)
lineage.fate: spent 2026-10-22 on measurement at the rework, never by a portal result (delivered 2026-10-12, pending review, left as delivered): the decisive step is reachable by one group-by on section_id, which names the call at an infinite lead in 300 of 300 swept world settings, and the designed forecast is linear in the in-service stock counts (regression on the twice-failed count alone R-squared 0.8180); re-rooted 2026-11-02 to architecture 2 in a new world, dataset and shell
lineage.niche: an electric distribution utility's underground cable program naming the one feeder whose worst sections it replaces in 2027, by the cable failures each feeder's in-service sections will have next year, when a first failure seldom recurs and a section that has failed twice keeps failing
lineage.driver: When a unit's coming events arise in its parts and a part that has already failed more than once keeps failing at many times the rate of a part with one or no failures, both the unit's trailing event rate and any rate built from its parts' visible attributes miss that the forward count is driven by the current mix of its parts' own failure histories; only a forecast that carries each part's prior failures forward names the unit with the most events ahead.
lineage.stump: A competent solver averages each feeder's last five years of cable-condition failures on the sections still in service and files Mill Lane 7 (about 14.4 a year against Quarry Hill 21's 10.4, fifth of eight), or applies failure rates by insulation and age and files Sutter Park 5; the step that lands it there is forecasting from feeder history or visible attributes when a section's next failure depends on how often it has already failed, and only Quarry Hill 21 carries in-service sections that have failed twice or more (17, heading 2027 at about 15 expected failures).
lineage.why: The correcting quantity was one per class (four pooled rates by prior-failure count), forced from the same file at the same grain as the main file, so a count of rows by section_id carried it; the re-root needs a correcting quantity one per case, forced by a second file at a finer grain, with no group-by on any shipped key reaching the call.

notes: Anomaly Detection & Diagnostics: separating where a recurring fault really is from where a device's record places it. The prompt asks where the patrol should look; no method is named. The physics forces the relocation (the apparent impedance of a fault is the cumulative impedance of the line to it, filed in the GIS and the construction standards), and the record's own locator is refuted only by recomputing it, a check no sentence asks for. Gap rule: no filed sentence says how a fault is located; G2 decisive (the locator works at the line grain, the answer needs the segment grain), G16 (the method the line's structure entitles), G3 (the recorded location against the fault's). Personas drawn with guard.py names (en_US, seed 183): Debbie Kline and Lisa Lawson, not the v1 personas.
